entries.title: Integral-Blade Table Tennis Paddle
entries.description: One original static low-poly table-tennis paddle with a broad thin faceted oval playing head, a narrowed neck and a long flat-ended handle cut as one continuous solid blade. Two separately editable tapered wooden-looking grip scales fully seat against the opposed handle faces. The front playing face is muted red and the back charcoal; these are assignments on the same closed blade surface, with honey wood on the complete finite edge and handle, not overlaid sheets or separate rubber skins. The entire paddle stands vertically on the complete three adjacent flat butt faces, with horizontal bounds centred and origin at ground. Three closed meshes, three opaque constant untextured PBR materials, one prop, zero scenes. All numeric shape coordinates newly authored; no old cutting board, palette, reflector, brush, trowel, mirror, table or bat geometry is imported, scaled, recoloured, extracted or assembled. Generic mesh-building, planar triangulation and export guards are reused. No hanging or thumb hole, net, ball, player, stand, logo, decorative text, texture, articulated joint, rig or animation. Stylized game-space appearance only: no regulation dimensions, sport affiliation, rubber specification, grip fit, bounce, spin, striking performance, collision physics, physical balance, stability, playability, manufacturing, material suitability, durability or safety certification.

entries.title: Continuous Toe-Blade Hockey Stick
entries.description: One original static low-poly ice-hockey-style stick appearance. A long narrow rectangular shaft descends continuously through an angular heel into a broad low lateral toe blade. The upper grip gently widens at the flat closed butt; the blade has a blunt bevelled toe silhouette and one long complete straight resting edge. The shaft, heel, toe and upper grip are one closed connected thick solid. Muted blue lower-blade, honey shaft and dark upper-grip regions are true face assignments within that one surface, without floating wraps or duplicate skins. One editable mesh, three opaque constant untextured PBR materials, one prop, zero scenes. The whole blade underside rests at ground Z0; horizontal bounds are centred, source Z up and presentation front -Y. Every numeric shape coordinate is newly authored. No old bat, paddle, axe, shovel, sickle, dibber or other model geometry is imported, stretched, scaled, recoloured, extracted or assembled. Generic mesh, finite planar triangulation and guarded export routines are reused. No opening, cavity, socket, separate joint, puck, ball, player, rink, logo, typography, texture, rig or animation. The fixed planar blade has no lateral playing curve or flex. Stylized game-space visual geometry only: no certified hockey dimensions, event affiliation, hand fit, grip, puck control, striking or rebound performance, balance, tipping resistance, physical stability, strength, material suitability, collision physics, manufacture, real equipment design, playability or safety certification.
